B1:
Touched fires once per touching part (both feet, legs, torso...) and repeatedly as contacts change, all within the same frame before Destroy takes effect, so several handlers run before the part is gone (Destroy doesn't stop events already queued; with deferred signals they all fire). Fix: a debounce flag set before granting:
```lua
local part = script.Parent
local collected = false
part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
	if collected then return end
	local plr = game.Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
	if not plr then return end
	local hum = hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
	collected = true
	plr.leaderstats.Coins.Value += 10
	part:Destroy()
end)
```
(For respawning coins use a per-player debounce table instead.)
B2: With StreamingEnabled the client only has parts near the player; far doors haven't streamed in when the LocalScript runs, so indexing `Hotel.Door` errors (and they can stream out later). Fix 1: wait for it: `local door = workspace.Map.Buildings.Hotel:WaitForChild("Door")` (with the whole path using WaitForChild, optionally with timeout, and handle it streaming out/being replaced). Fix 2 (better for many doors): tag doors with CollectionService and use `CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal("Door")` plus `GetTagged`, connecting Touched when each door streams in and disconnecting on GetInstanceRemovedSignal. Alternatively set the Hotel model's ModelStreamingMode = Persistent (always sent to clients) or Atomic, or handle door touches on the server.
B3: Bugs: (1) plr can be nil if the player left; plr.UserId errors inside pcall, so ok = false. (2) The pcall result is ignored: it returns PurchaseGranted even when the save failed -> charged, nothing received. (3) No PurchaseId dedupe -> Roblox retries the receipt (timeout, rejoin, another server) and coins are added twice. (4) GetAsync + SetAsync is a non-atomic read-modify-write; use UpdateAsync. (5) Coins don't update the live session data, and it ignores ProductId. Corrected: if player missing -> NotProcessedYet; route by info.ProductId; in one UpdateAsync on the player's profile, check a stored processed-receipt list for info.PurchaseId, if absent add 100 coins and record the PurchaseId (cap list size); only if the update succeeds return PurchaseGranted (also if already recorded); any error -> NotProcessedYet. Update the in-memory/leaderstats value after success. Assign ProcessReceipt only once.
B4: Remotes serialize values: tables are copied as plain data, so metatables (and functions) are stripped; the client gets {Name='Rifle', Ammo=30} without the Weapon metatable, so w:Fire is nil. Instance arguments are sent as references, and an Instance the client can't see (ServerStorage isn't replicated) arrives as nil. Fix: send plain data (e.g. a weapon id/state) and reconstruct on the client with a shared ModuleScript in ReplicatedStorage: `local w = setmetatable(data, Weapon)` (or Weapon.new(data)). For the part, put Muzzle somewhere replicated (ReplicatedStorage/Workspace) first, or clone it into a replicated location, or send its data (CFrame, name) instead.
B5:
workspace:Raycast's second argument is the full direction vector, whose length is the ray distance. Passing .Unit gives a 1-stud ray, so it only hits things within a stud. Fix: multiply by range (or use target - origin directly), and exclude the shooter:
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {shooterCharacter}
local dir = (target - origin).Unit * 500
local r = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
if r then print(r.Instance, r.Position) end
```
B6: When the last player leaves (or the server shuts down), the server closes and may terminate before PlayerRemoving's yielding SetAsync finishes, so the write is killed. Fix: game:BindToClose to save every remaining player's data before shutdown (in parallel with task.spawn, waiting until all finish, within the ~30s limit), plus regular autosaves; make saving idempotent so PlayerRemoving and BindToClose don't double-write conflicting data (track saved/in-progress players), and prefer UpdateAsync with session locking. In Studio, BindToClose saves can be skipped/shortened.
B7:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local remote = game.ReplicatedStorage.Remotes.UseAbility
local COOLDOWN = 2
local lastUse = {} -- [Player] = time

remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, abilityId)
	if typeof(abilityId) ~= "string" or not Abilities[abilityId] then return end
	local now = os.clock()
	local last = lastUse[player]
	if last and now - last < COOLDOWN then return end -- silently drop spam
	local char = player.Character
	local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
	lastUse[player] = now
	Abilities[abilityId](player, char)
end)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	lastUse[player] = nil -- no leak
end)
```
The cooldown is server time only; the client's own cooldown UI is cosmetic.
B8:
```lua
local MPS = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local store = game:GetService("DataStoreService"):GetDataStore("PlayerData")
local GEMS100 = 123456
local handlers = { [GEMS100] = function(data) data.Gems = (data.Gems or 0) + 100 end }

MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info)
	local handler = handlers[info.ProductId]
	if not handler then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
	local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
	if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
	local granted = false
	local ok, err = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, "player_" .. info.PlayerId, function(data)
		data = data or {Gems = 0}
		data.Receipts = data.Receipts or {}
		if data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] then granted = true return nil end -- already done
		handler(data)
		data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] = os.time()
		granted = true
		return data
	end)
	if not ok or not granted then
		warn("Receipt failed", info.PurchaseId, err)
		return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet
	end
	-- update live session/leaderstats here
	return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end
```
(Note: set granted inside the transform only as last-call state; reset it at the start of each call. Prune old receipt ids. With a session-locked profile system, write into the loaded profile and save it instead.) Assign ProcessReceipt once; never grant in PromptProductPurchaseFinished.

local function closeMenu()

	local t = TweenService:Create(menu, info, {Position = CLOSED})

		end
	end)
	t:Play()

B10:
```lua
local MAX_RANGE = 200
local DAMAGE = 20

local function shoot(player: Player, targetPos: Vector3)
	if typeof(targetPos) ~= "Vector3" or targetPos ~= targetPos then return end
	local char = player.Character
	local head = char and char:FindFirstChild("Head")
	local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if not head or not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
	local origin = head.Position
	local offset = targetPos - origin
	if offset.Magnitude < 1e-3 then return end
	local params = RaycastParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {char}
	local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, offset.Unit * MAX_RANGE, params)
	if not result then return end
	local model = result.Instance:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
	local targetHum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if targetHum and targetHum.Health > 0 then
		targetHum:TakeDamage(DAMAGE)
	end
end
```

B11:
```lua
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local TAG = "KillBrick"
local connections = {}

local function onAdded(part)
	if not part:IsA("BasePart") or connections[part] then return end
	connections[part] = part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
		local hum = hit.Parent and hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
		if hum and hum.Health > 0 then hum.Health = 0 end
	end)
end

local function onRemoved(part)
	local c = connections[part]
	if c then c:Disconnect() connections[part] = nil end
end

CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(TAG):Connect(onAdded)
CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(TAG):Connect(onRemoved)
for _, p in CollectionService:GetTagged(TAG) do onAdded(p) end
```
(Removed signal also fires when a tagged part is destroyed, so the table doesn't leak.)

```lua
local TeleportService = game:GetService("TeleportService")
local MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
local RETRY_DELAY = 2

local function safeTeleport(placeId, players, teleportData)
	local options = Instance.new("TeleportOptions")
	if teleportData then options:SetTeleportData(teleportData) end
	for attempt = 1, MAX_ATTEMPTS do
		local ok, result = pcall(TeleportService.TeleportAsync, TeleportService, placeId, players, options)
		if ok then return true, result end
		warn("TeleportAsync failed:", result)
		task.wait(RETRY_DELAY * attempt)
	end
	return false

	if result == Enum.TeleportResult.Flooded or result == Enum.TeleportResult.Failure
		or result == Enum.TeleportResult.Unauthorized then
		-- transient: retry after a delay
		task.wait(RETRY_DELAY)
		safeTeleport(placeId, {player}, options and options:GetTeleportData())
	else
		warn("Teleport failed for", player, result, errorMessage)
	end
end)
```
Add a per-player retry counter to avoid infinite retry loops; teleportData is client-visible, never trust it for currency.
B13: (a) Buy: client -> server via a RemoteEvent (or a RemoteFunction invoked by the client if the UI needs an immediate success/fail reply) sending only the item id. The server owns the coin balance and the price list, validates (item exists, affordable, rate limit), deducts and grants. (b) Counter update: server -> client via replicated state (leaderstats IntValue / player Attribute, which the client listens to with Changed/GetAttributeChangedSignal) or a RemoteEvent:FireClient. Don't use RemoteFunction:InvokeClient: the server would yield on the client, a malicious or disconnected client can make it hang forever or error, and the client's reply can't be trusted; the server doesn't need an answer for a UI update, so a one-way event/replicated value is correct.
B14: Teleport data (TeleportOptions:SetTeleportData) travels via the client and is readable/modifiable by exploiters, so it is fine only for non-sensitive, cosmetic or routing info (e.g. chosen loadout id, match id, party info), and must still be validated on arrival. The coin balance is authoritative data: keep it in DataStores (with session locking: save/release before teleport, load in the match place), and use MemoryStore (short-lived, fast, shared across servers) for transient per-match state like the reserved-server code, matchmaking queues, or the loadout keyed by userId with a TTL. Choice: coins via DataStore (session-locked profile), loadout via MemoryStore or validated teleport data (validate against owned items from the DataStore), never trust teleport data for currency.
B15: Per-instance Scripts (610 copies) are hard to maintain (fixing a bug means editing every copy), cost memory and startup time, duplicate connections and state, and break on streamed/spawned instances. Recommended: tag instances with CollectionService (Door, Pickup, Turret) and have one server Script/module per behaviour (plus client modules for visuals) that binds to GetTagged and GetInstanceAddedSignal, and cleans up on GetInstanceRemovedSignal (disconnect connections, a per-instance state/Janitor table). Configuration via Attributes on each instance. Newly spawned instances get the tag (e.g. from templates) and are picked up by the added signal; on the client, streamed-in instances fire the added signal when they arrive and the removed signal when streamed out, so clients handle streaming naturally. Turrets can share one Heartbeat loop over a set instead of 60 loops.
B16: Give the driver network ownership of the car's assembly (VehicleSeat occupant -> seat:SetNetworkOwner(player) on sit, back to server/nil on exit) for responsive physics without input lag. Risk: the owner simulates and replicates the physics, so an exploiter can teleport, speed-hack, fly the car, or fling other players with it. Server must still validate: sanity-check speed/position deltas and acceleration (reset or reclaim ownership on violation), checkpoint order and lap times (race results computed server-side), only seated drivers own a car, and spawning/purchasing cars and collisions/damage are server-decided. Disable auto ownership changes (SetNetworkOwnershipAuto off) when needed.
B17: Use UnreliableRemoteEvent for high-frequency, latest-value-wins data like aim direction/position. Constraints: no delivery or ordering guarantee (packets can drop or arrive out of order), payload limit ~1000 bytes per call (larger is dropped), and throttling under bursts. Handle: send compact data (numbers, quantize/compress the direction, e.g. buffer or Vector3int16), include a sequence number or timestamp and ignore older packets, reduce frequency (send only on change/10-20 Hz) and interpolate on receivers, keep important one-off events (shots, hits) on a reliable RemoteEvent, and validate/rate-limit on the server. Character position is already replicated, so don't send it.
B18: Split NPCs across several Actors (e.g. 8-16, each owning a batch of NPC scripts/models, or a pooled worker script under each Actor). In each actor, run the work in parallel: RunService.Heartbeat:ConnectParallel (or task.desynchronize) to do raycasts, distance checks and path scoring (reads and spatial queries are allowed in parallel); collect results; then task.synchronize() to apply writes (move to, CFrame/property changes, firing events). Limitations: most instance property writes and many APIs are unsafe in parallel and require synchronize; scripts can only modify instances under their own Actor; data between actors is copied (Actor:SendMessage, SharedTable for shared state); module state isn't shared between actors (each requires its own copy); overhead of sync points, so batch per frame; pathfinding ComputeAsync yields (do it serially/staggered); always profile with the MicroProfiler. Also stagger updates over frames and reduce frequency for distant NPCs.
B19: Enable Workspace.StreamingEnabled. Sensible settings: StreamingMinRadius ~64-128, StreamingTargetRadius ~256-1024 (default 64/1024), StreamOutBehavior = Opportunistic (or LowMemory), StreamingIntegrityMode = PauseOutsideLoadedArea or MinimumRadiusPause to avoid falling into unloaded world; use ModelStreamingMode Atomic for models that must arrive whole, Persistent only for a few always-needed models (sparingly, increases memory), and Player.RequestStreamAroundAsync before teleporting players. Scripts: client code must not assume parts exist: use WaitForChild (with timeouts) or, better, CollectionService tags with added/removed signals, handle instances streaming out (disconnect, nil checks), and keep server logic server-side (server always has everything). Also reduce part counts and texture memory.
B20: Saving 80 players every 5s is ~960 SetAsync per minute from one server, a large chunk of the experience write budget (300 + 20 x CCU per minute, shared by all servers and Open Cloud; per server 60 + 40 x players), and all fired on the same tick, so the request queue (30 per type) overflows: 302 is the SetAsync queue-full throttle and dropped requests mean lost saves; per-key write rate also caps saves to the same key (roughly once every 6s). Better: keep data in a session cache, mark it dirty on change, autosave every 60-300s per player with staggered/jittered offsets, only if dirty; use UpdateAsync with session locking (or ProfileStore); save on PlayerRemoving and in BindToClose; retry with exponential backoff and check GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before writing; keep profiles small.
B21: In Studio, open the Assistant panel, the ... (more) menu > Manage MCP Servers, and turn on 'Enable Studio as MCP server' (then connect the external client, e.g. Claude Code). Tools it exposes include: script_read, multi_edit, script_search, script_grep, search_game_tree, inspect_instance, execute_luau, get_studio_state, start_stop_play, get_console_output, screen_capture, character_navigation, user_keyboard_input, user_mouse_input, generate_mesh, generate_material, insert_asset, search_asset, list_roblox_studios.
B22: Three core instances: InputContext (a group/layer of actions that can be enabled/disabled, with a Priority and Sink), InputAction (the abstract action, with a Type such as Bool, Direction1D/2D/3D, ViewportPosition), and InputBinding (maps a physical input to the action: KeyCode, gamepad buttons/thumbsticks, or a UIButton for touch). A Bool action signals a press through its Pressed and Released events (and StateChanged with the new value; GetState to poll). Menu precedence: put menu actions in a separate InputContext with a higher Priority than the default player scripts' contexts and Sink = true, and enable it when the menu opens (disable on close), so its bindings consume the input before lower-priority contexts (movement/jump) receive it.
B23: Roblox's UI Styling system (Style Editor) applies CSS-like rules to GuiObjects. Main instances: StyleSheet (a container of rules, also used as a token/theme sheet), StyleRule (has a Selector, e.g. class name, .tag, #Name, state like :hover, and property values via SetProperty/SetProperties; can nest and has Priority), StyleLink (parented under a ScreenGui/LayerCollector or GuiObject with StyleSheet pointing at a sheet, which applies the sheet to that subtree), StyleDerive (lets a sheet inherit rules from another sheet), and StyleQuery (conditional rules by size/input). Styles reach UI when a StyleLink connects the sheet to the UI tree and selectors match instances (by ClassName, tags via CollectionService-style tags, or name); matched properties override defaults. Tokens: define attributes on a token StyleSheet (e.g. PrimaryColor), derive it into your sheet, and reference them in rule values as "$PrimaryColor"; swapping the token sheet (StyleDerive) changes themes everywhere.
B24: Roblox requires an age check to use chat: facial age estimation via the camera (processed by a vendor, Persona; images deleted after) or ID verification for 13+ users; rolled out from late 2025 and required globally from January 2026. Users are placed in age groups: under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20, and 21+. Users can chat only with their own and adjacent age groups (e.g. 13-15 can chat with 9-12 and 16-17, but not adults 18+), with 'Trusted Connections' allowing wider chat for people known in real life; under-9s have chat off by default unless a parent consents. Unchecked users can't use chat. Developers should use TextChatService (respects these rules automatically; CanUsersDirectChatAsync / chat group APIs) and never build chat over RemoteEvents.
